title: DynaMoGe: Extending Metric Monocular Geometry Estimation to Dynamic Scenes via Temporal Consistency and Motion Decomposition
description:
Problem: MoGe-2 excels at metric 3D reconstruction from single static images, but real-world video contains dynamic objects (people, vehicles) that violate the static scene assumption, causing artifacts and temporal inconsistency when applied frame-by-frame. No existing method simultaneously achieves metric scale, fine-grained detail, and temporally coherent geometry for dynamic monocular video.

Proposed Method: We extend MoGe-2 with a lightweight temporal module that (1) decomposes scenes into static background and dynamic foreground via a motion segmentation head trained jointly with geometry, (2) enforces metric-consistent temporal smoothness on static regions using a cross-frame geometric consistency loss, and (3) predicts per-object relative motion fields for dynamic regions, maintaining accurate metric geometry locally. The data refinement pipeline from MoGe-2 is extended to video datasets by propagating synthetic sharp labels temporally using optical flow.

Experiments: We evaluate on KITTI, Sintel, and TUM-RGBD for metric depth accuracy and temporal consistency (OPW metric). Ablations isolate contributions of motion decomposition, temporal loss, and video data refinement. Qualitative results demonstrate artifact-free, temporally coherent metric point maps on in-the-wild driving and indoor videos. We compare against NVDS, ChronoDepth, and frame-wise MoGe-2 baselines.

title: DynaMoGe: Extending Metric Monocular Geometry Estimation to Dynamic Scenes via Temporal Consistency and Motion Decoupling
description: Problem: MoGe-2 produces high-quality metric 3D point maps from single images but treats each frame independently, ignoring temporal structure in video. Dynamic scenes with moving objects cause inconsistent geometry estimates across frames, limiting downstream applications like video reconstruction, scene flow estimation, and AR/VR. Proposed Method: We extend MoGe-2 to video by introducing a temporal consistency module that enforces metric-scale coherence across frames. Specifically, we (1) augment the architecture with a lightweight cross-frame attention mechanism operating on adjacent point maps, encouraging temporally smooth static backgrounds; (2) decouple moving objects from the static scene using a motion segmentation head trained jointly with geometry, allowing independent but consistent treatment of dynamic regions; and (3) develop a self-supervised temporal regularization loss that penalizes rigid-body inconsistencies in static regions between consecutive frames using ego-motion alignment. For training, we curate video datasets (KITTI, Waymo, Sintel, Kubric) with ground-truth depth sequences and augment synthetic labels using MoGe-2's refinement pipeline to maintain fine-grained detail. Experiments: We evaluate on KITTI Eigen split, NYUv2 video sequences, ScanNet, and Sintel depth benchmarks, reporting per-frame accuracy, temporal consistency metrics (OPW, temporal RMSE), and scene flow accuracy compared to prior video depth and scene flow baselines.

description: Problem: MoGe-2 achieves impressive single-frame metric geometry reconstruction but treats each frame independently, making it unsuitable for video inputs where temporal consistency and moving objects cause flickering artifacts and geometrically inconsistent depth sequences. Dynamic scene understanding from monocular video remains a critical open challenge. Proposed Method: We extend MoGe-2 to video by introducing a lightweight temporal consistency module that aggregates features across adjacent frames using a sliding-window attention mechanism operating on predicted point maps. We additionally propose a motion decomposition head that explicitly separates static background geometry (aligned with metric scale) from dynamic foreground objects, using optical flow supervision to disentangle ego-motion from object motion. A temporal refinement loss enforces geometric consistency between overlapping predictions while allowing legitimate motion. The static background is accumulated into a coherent metric scene representation using incremental fusion. Experiments: We evaluate on KITTI-360, Waymo, and ScanNet video benchmarks measuring temporal consistency (OPW metric), metric depth accuracy (AbsRel, δ1), and dynamic object handling (segmentation-conditioned depth error). Ablations isolate contributions of temporal attention, motion decomposition, and the flow supervision. We also demonstrate downstream benefits for monocular SLAM and novel view synthesis of dynamic scenes.

title: DynoGe: Extending Metric Monocular Geometry Estimation to Dynamic Scenes via Temporal Consistency and Motion Decomposition
description:

First, we add a lightweight motion segmentation head trained on synthetic dynamic scenes to produce per-pixel motion masks. Second, we propose a temporal consistency loss that enforces smooth point map evolution for static regions across frames while allowing independent motion for dynamic objects. Third, we adopt a two-stream architecture: a scene stream (MoGe-2 backbone frozen) for static geometry, and a dynamic object stream that estimates object-relative metric depth independently, then composites the two using the motion mask. Data refinement from MoGe-2 is extended to include synthetic dynamic sequences (e.g., rendered CARLA, Kubric) to provide sharp ground-truth labels for moving objects.

Experiments: Evaluate on KITTI-360 (outdoor driving), Sintel (optical flow + depth), and PointOdyssey (dynamic people). Metrics include AbsRel, δ1 for static/dynamic regions separately, temporal smoothness (OPW), and novel view synthesis quality (PSNR/SSIM) from reconstructed 4D point clouds.

title: MoGe-Temporal: Consistent Metric Geometry Estimation Across Video Sequences via Cross-Frame Geometric Coherence
description: Problem: MoGe-2 produces accurate per-frame metric geometry but processes frames independently, leading to temporal inconsistencies (flickering depth, scale drift) that undermine downstream applications like video 3D reconstruction, novel view synthesis, and AR/VR. Extending single-image metric geometry to temporally coherent video geometry remains unsolved without sacrificing single-frame accuracy. Proposed Method: We introduce a lightweight temporal coherence module on top of a frozen MoGe-2 backbone. The module employs: (1) a cross-frame feature aggregation mechanism using deformable attention over nearby frames' point map features, warped via estimated optical flow, to enforce geometric consistency; (2) a scale-drift correction layer that aligns metric scale predictions across frames using overlapping point correspondences and a differentiable least-squares solver; and (3) a temporal smoothness regularization loss that penalizes inconsistencies in overlapping regions while preserving sharp static details. Only the temporal module is trained, preserving MoGe-2's strong single-frame priors. Planned Experiments: We evaluate on ScanNetV2, TUM RGB-D, and KITTI Depth using temporal consistency metrics (OPW, scale drift), standard depth metrics (AbsRel, δ1), and downstream tasks including monocular visual odometry and video NeRF reconstruction quality, comparing against MoGe-2 per-frame baselines and video depth methods like DepthCrafter and ChronoDepth.

title: TemporalMoGe: Consistent Metric Geometry Estimation Across Video Sequences via Temporal Point Map Propagation
description: Problem: While MoGe-2 achieves impressive single-image metric geometry estimation, applying it independently to video frames produces temporally inconsistent depth maps with flickering artifacts and drift in metric scale across frames—critical failures for downstream applications like video-based 3D reconstruction, AR/VR, and autonomous navigation. Proposed Method: We extend MoGe-2 to video by introducing a Temporal Point Map Propagation (TPMP) module that enforces geometric consistency across frames. Specifically, we (1) warp previous-frame metric point maps into the current frame using estimated optical flow and camera motion, (2) fuse the warped prior with the per-frame MoGe-2 prediction via a lightweight attention-based consistency gating network, and (3) apply a temporal metric scale calibration loss that penalizes scale drift in overlapping regions across consecutive frames. The model is fine-tuned end-to-end using frozen MoGe-2 weights as a backbone, training only the temporal fusion module on video datasets (ScanNetV2, Waymo, TartanAir). Experiments: We evaluate on standard video depth benchmarks (Sintel, KITTI-360, NYUv2-video) measuring temporal consistency metrics (OPW, flickering index), absolute metric accuracy (AbsRel, δ1), and downstream novel view synthesis quality (PSNR/SSIM). We compare against per-frame MoGe-2, Depth-Anything-V2 video variant, and NVDS.

title: DynoGe: Extending Metric Monocular Geometry Estimation to Dynamic Scenes via Temporal Consistency Regularization
description: Problem: MoGe-2 excels at static scene geometry from single images, but real-world applications (robotics, AR/VR, autonomous driving) involve dynamic scenes where moving objects violate static-world assumptions. Third, we develop a dynamic-object refinement module that estimates per-object rigid motion (6-DoF) and composites consistent object-level geometry across frames. We fine-tune from MoGe-2 weights on dynamic scene datasets (KITTI, Waymo, Sintel, Dynamic Replica) augmented with flow-based pseudo-labels. Experiments: We evaluate on (1) per-frame metric depth accuracy on dynamic benchmarks, (2) temporal consistency metrics (TC-Depth, TDV), (3) moving object 3D trajectory reconstruction, and (4) downstream application in monocular video 3D reconstruction. We compare against DUSt3R, MonST3R, and DepthCrafter baselines.

title: TemporalMoGe: Consistent Metric Geometry Estimation Across Video Sequences via Temporal Coherence Distillation
description:

Experiments: We evaluate on standard video depth benchmarks (ScanNetV2, KITTI Eigen splits, Bonn RGB-D Dynamic) using temporal consistency metrics (OPW, AbsRel over time, scale variance). We compare against per-frame MoGe-2, DepthCrafter, and MonST3R. Ablations examine window size, distillation weight schedules, and synthetic video dataset composition. We also demonstrate downstream benefits in video-based 3D reconstruction and novel view synthesis quality.
